title: Finnable raises Rs 405 Cr in Series C to expand multi-product lending
summary: Digital lender Finnable raised 405 crore rupees in Series C funding
detailed: Fintech company Finnable raised Rs 405 crore in a Series C funding round led by Bharat Value Fund, Pratithi Investments, and NKSquared.
The company's assets under management exceeded Rs 4,600 crore in October 2026, and its April-to-September profit after tax reached Rs 51 crore.
Finnable operates personal loans for salaried professionals, secured loans against property (LAP) for small businesses, and instant consumer finance checkout partnerships.
The newly raised funds will be used to expand the LAP business into new geographies, scale consumer finance partnerships, strengthen technology, and invest in AI.
sentences: Fintech company Finnable has raised Rs 405 crore in a Series C round.
The new investors are Bharat Value Fund, part of the Pantomath Group, along with Pratithi Investments and NKSquared.
Pratithi is the investment vehicle of Infosys co-founder Kris Gopalakrishnan's family, and NKSquared is the firm of Zerodha co-founders Nithin and Nikhil Kamath.
Existing backers Z47, TVS Capital and Claypond Capital continue in the company.
TVS Capital and Claypond Capital put in more money in this round.
The Rs 405 crore figure carries an asterisk in the company's release.
A disclaimer says final allotments and regulatory filings are still being completed and the figure is subject to final subscription numbers.
Finnable said its assets under management crossed Rs 4,600 crore in October 2026.
It reported a profit after tax of Rs 51 crore for April to September 2026, which already exceeds the Rs 46 crore it earned in the whole of FY26.
On asset quality, the company said its latest PAR 90 at six months on books stands at 0.24%.
This measures loans overdue by more than 90 days among those that have been on the books for six months.
Finnable pairs digital loan journeys and technology-led credit assessment with in-house collections.
Finnable runs three businesses.
Its personal loans target salaried professionals, mainly in metros and Tier I cities.
Its loan against property (LAP) business offers secured credit to small business owners in Tier II and Tier IV markets.
Its consumer finance arm provides instant checkout credit on leading e-commerce platforms, giving it access to younger, digitally active customers.
The company said it combines on-book lending with co-lending partnerships, which co-founder Amit Arora described as a capital-efficient model built to hold up across credit cycles.
The funds will go towards taking the LAP business into new geographies, scaling consumer finance partnerships and strengthening technology.
Finnable also plans to keep investing in AI across underwriting, fraud detection, collections and customer service.
Over the past year the company has also reinforced its board.
It has appointed Shrimohan Yadav, a former chief general manager at the Reserve Bank of India, and Sreeram R.
Iyer, a former global COO of the corporate and institutional business at ANZ Banking Group.
The most recent addition is Sekhar Garisa, managing director at Claypond Capital.
